original_question: Is the maximal abelian extension Qab of the rational numbers Q an ample field, where a field K is called ample when every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points, equivalently when K satisfies the other equivalent conditions listed in Proposition 2.1?
target_in_paper: Section 3 ("Algebraic fields"): the unnumbered open problem asking whether the maximal abelian extension Q^{ab} of Q is ample.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the specific field Q^{ab}, the property under discussion (ampleness/large-field property), and the paper’s curve-theoretic definition of an ample field. It is very close to the paper’s actual open problem in the algebraic-fields section.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, Q^{ab} should be identified explicitly as the maximal abelian extension of Q, usually inside a fixed algebraic closure \overline{Q}.
The paper treats "ample" and "large" as synonymous terminology; naming that synonym would make the question more paper-faithful.

The reference to "the other equivalent conditions listed in Proposition 2.1" is not self-contained; for a stand-alone question, either one criterion should be stated explicitly or the proposition reference should be removed.

If one wants the formulation to be fully self-contained and faithful to the nearby context, one may note that for Q this field is also the maximal cyclotomic extension (Kronecker-Weber), though the paper’s question is posed for Q^{ab}.

No extra hypotheses such as genus bounds, characteristic assumptions beyond the base field being Q^{ab}, or additional finiteness assumptions are part of the paper’s question; the scope is exactly this one field and the standard notion of ampleness.
refined_question: Let Q^{ab} \subseteq \overline{Q} be the maximal abelian extension of the rational numbers Q. Is Q^{ab} an ample (equivalently, large) field; that is, does every smooth curve C over Q^{ab} with C(Q^{ab}) \neq \varnothing have infinitely many Q^{ab}-rational points?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Proposition 2.1, is Q^{ab} a large field in the sense that every smooth Q^{ab}-variety with a Q^{ab}-rational point has Zariski-dense Q^{ab}-rational points?
justification: The draft is targeting the specific open problem in the paper’s section on algebraic fields, not a broader neighboring problem. The nearby background proposition supplies the equivalent formulations of ampleness/large-fieldness, so the only real issue with the draft is that it refers back to Proposition 2.1 instead of stating the question fully on its own. The refined version keeps exactly the same mathematical scope as the paper: one fixed field, Q^{ab}, and the standard ampleness property, with no extra hypotheses or generalization.
